ei.title: Chapter 3-09: The Scarcity of Time and Human Choice
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: Action takes place by choosing which ends shall be satisfied by the employment of means. Time is scarce for man only because whichever ends he chooses to satisfy, there are others that must remain unsatisfied. When we must use a means so that some ends remain unsatisfied, the necessity for a choice among ends arises. For example, Jones is engaged in watching a baseball game on television. He is faced with the choice of spending the next hour in: continuing to watch the baseball game, playing bridge, or going for a drive. He would like to do all three of these things, but his means (time) is insufficient. As a result, he must choose; one end can be satisfied, but the others must go unfulfilled. Suppose that he decides on course A. This is a clear indication that he has ranked the satisfaction of end A higher than the satisfaction of ends B or C.

questions.passage: Action takes place by choosing which ends shall be satisfied by the employment of means. Time is (A)[scarce / abundant] for man only because whichever ends he chooses to satisfy, there are others that must remain (B)[unsatisfied / fulfilled]. When we must use a means so that some ends remain unsatisfied, the necessity for a choice among ends arises. For example, Jones is engaged in watching a baseball game on television. He is faced with the choice of spending the next hour in: continuing to watch the baseball game, playing bridge, or going for a drive. He would like to do all three of these things, but his means (time) is (C)[insufficient / sufficient]. As a result, he must choose; one end can be satisfied, but the others must go unfulfilled. Suppose that he decides on course A. This is a clear indication that he has ranked the satisfaction of end A higher than the satisfaction of ends B or C.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 시간은 부족하고, 다른 목적은 충족되지 않은 채 남으며, 수단은 불충분하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① abundant — unsatisfied — insufficient (A 반대: 부족한→풍부한)
❌ ② scarce — fulfilled — insufficient (B 반대: 충족되지 않은→충족된)
✅ ③ scarce — unsatisfied — insufficient — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ scarce — unsatisfied — sufficient (C 반대: 불충분한→충분한)
det.tip: scarce(부족한) ↔ abundant(풍부한), unsatisfied(충족되지 않은) ↔ fulfilled(충족된)

questions.passage: Action takes place by choosing which ends shall be (A)[satisfied / frustrated] by the employment of means. Time is scarce for man only because whichever ends he chooses to satisfy, there are others that must remain unsatisfied. When we must use a means so that some ends remain unsatisfied, the necessity for a choice among ends (B)[arises / disappears]. For example, Jones is engaged in watching a baseball game on television. He is faced with the choice of spending the next hour in: continuing to watch the baseball game, playing bridge, or going for a drive. He would like to do all three of these things, but his means (time) is insufficient. As a result, he must choose; one end can be satisfied, but the others must go (C)[unfulfilled / completed]. Suppose that he decides on course A. This is a clear indication that he has ranked the satisfaction of end A higher than the satisfaction of ends B or C.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 어떤 목적이 충족되고, 선택의 필요성이 생기며, 나머지는 미충족 상태로 남는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① satisfied — arises — unfulfilled — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② frustrated — arises — unfulfilled (A 반대: 충족된→좌절된)
❌ ③ satisfied — disappears — unfulfilled (B 반대: 발생하다→사라지다)
❌ ④ satisfied — arises — completed (C 반대: 미충족→완료된)
det.tip: arises(발생하다) ↔ disappears(사라지다), unfulfilled(미충족) ↔ completed(완료된)

questions.passage: Action takes place by choosing which ends shall be satisfied by the (A)[employment / abandonment] of means. Time is scarce for man only because whichever ends he chooses to satisfy, there are others that must remain unsatisfied. When we must use a means so that some ends remain unsatisfied, the necessity for a choice among ends arises. For example, Jones is (B)[engaged / bored] in watching a baseball game on television. He is faced with the choice of spending the next hour in: continuing to watch the baseball game, playing bridge, or going for a drive. He would like to do all three of these things, but his means (time) is insufficient. As a result, he must choose; one end can be satisfied, but the others must go unfulfilled. Suppose that he decides on course A. This is a clear indication that he has (C)[ranked / ignored] the satisfaction of end A higher than the satisfaction of ends B or C.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 수단의 사용을 통해, Jones는 야구 관람에 몰두하며, 만족도의 순위를 매겼다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① abandonment — engaged — ranked (A 반대: 사용→포기)
❌ ② employment — bored — ranked (B 반대: 몰두한→지루한)
❌ ③ employment — engaged — ignored (C 반대: 순위를 매기다→무시하다)
✅ ④ employment — engaged — ranked — 원문 일치 ←정답
det.tip: employment(사용, 이용) ↔ abandonment(포기), engaged(몰두한) ↔ bored(지루한)

questions.passage: Action takes place by ①<u>choosing</u> which ends shall be satisfied by the employment of means. Time is scarce for man only because whichever ends he chooses to ②<u>abandon</u>, there are others that must remain unsatisfied. When we must use a means so that some ends remain unsatisfied, the ③<u>necessity</u> for a choice among ends arises. For example, Jones is engaged in watching a baseball game on television. He is faced with the choice of spending the next hour in: continuing to watch the baseball game, playing bridge, or going for a drive. He would like to do all three of these things, but his means (time) is ④<u>insufficient</u>. As a result, he must choose; one end can be satisfied, but the others must go unfulfilled. Suppose that he decides on course A. This is a clear indication that he has ranked the satisfaction of end A higher than the satisfaction of ends B or C.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
① <u>choosing</u> (선택하는) — 어떤 목적을 충족할지 선택한다는 맥락에 적절
② <u>abandon</u> (포기하다) — 원문은 satisfy(충족시키다). 어떤 목적을 충족시키기로 선택하면 다른 것이 남는다는 맥락에서 abandon은 부적절 ←정답
③ <u>necessity</u> (필요성) — 선택의 필요성이 생긴다는 맥락에 적절
④ <u>insufficient</u> (불충분한) — 수단(시간)이 불충분하다는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: satisfy(충족시키다) ↔ abandon(포기하다)

questions.passage: Action takes place by choosing which ends shall be satisfied by the employment of means. Time is ①<u>plentiful</u> for man only because whichever ends he chooses to satisfy, there are others that must remain unsatisfied. When we must use a means so that some ends remain unsatisfied, the necessity for a choice among ends ②<u>arises</u>. For example, Jones is engaged in watching a baseball game on television. He is ③<u>faced</u> with the choice of spending the next hour in: continuing to watch the baseball game, playing bridge, or going for a drive. He would like to do all three of these things, but his means (time) is insufficient. As a result, he must choose; one end can be satisfied, but the others must go unfulfilled. Suppose that he decides on course A. This is a clear indication that he has ④<u>ranked</u> the satisfaction of end A higher than the satisfaction of ends B or C.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
① <u>plentiful</u> (풍부한) — 원문은 scarce(부족한). 시간이 부족하기 때문에 선택해야 한다는 논지에서 plentiful은 부적절 ←정답
② <u>arises</u> (발생하다) — 선택의 필요성이 발생한다는 맥락에 적절
③ <u>faced</u> (직면한) — 선택에 직면한다는 맥락에 적절
④ <u>ranked</u> (순위를 매긴) — 만족도 순위를 매겼다는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: scarce(부족한) ↔ plentiful(풍부한, 충분한)

questions.passage: Action takes place by choosing which ends shall be satisfied by the ①<u>employment</u> of means. Time is scarce for man only because whichever ends he chooses to satisfy, there are others that must ②<u>remain</u> unsatisfied. When we must use a means so that some ends remain unsatisfied, the necessity for a choice among ends arises. For example, Jones is engaged in watching a baseball game on television. He is faced with the choice of spending the next hour in: continuing to watch the baseball game, playing bridge, or going for a drive. He would like to do all three of these things, but his means (time) is ③<u>excessive</u>. As a result, he must choose; one end can be satisfied, but the others must go unfulfilled. Suppose that he decides on course A. This is a clear ④<u>indication</u> that he has ranked the satisfaction of end A higher than the satisfaction of ends B or C.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
① <u>employment</u> (사용) — 수단의 사용을 통해 행동한다는 맥락에 적절
② <u>remain</u> (남아 있다) — 다른 목적이 미충족 상태로 남는다는 맥락에 적절
③ <u>excessive</u> (과도한) — 원문은 insufficient(불충분한). 수단(시간)이 불충분하여 선택해야 한다는 맥락에서 excessive는 부적절 ←정답
④ <u>indication</u> (표시) — 명확한 표시라는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: insufficient(불충분한) ↔ excessive(과도한)

questions.passage: Action takes place by choosing which ends shall be satisfied by the employment of means. Time is __________ for man only because whichever ends he chooses to satisfy, there are others that must remain unsatisfied. When we must use a means so that some ends remain unsatisfied, the necessity for a choice among ends arises. For example, Jones is engaged in watching a baseball game on television. He is faced with the choice of spending the next hour in: continuing to watch the baseball game, playing bridge, or going for a drive. He would like to do all three of these things, but his means (time) is insufficient. As a result, he must choose; one end can be satisfied, but the others must go unfulfilled. Suppose that he decides on course A. This is a clear indication that he has ranked the satisfaction of end A higher than the satisfaction of ends B or C.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① abundant (풍부한) — 반대 의미. 시간이 풍부하면 선택할 필요가 없음
❌ ② unlimited (무한한) — 반대 의미. 시간이 무한하면 모든 것을 할 수 있음
❌ ③ available (이용 가능한) — 시간이 이용 가능하다는 것은 부족함을 나타내지 않음
✅ ④ scarce (부족한) — 시간이 부족하기 때문에 하나를 선택하면 나머지를 포기해야 한다는 원문 맥락에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: scarce = insufficient, rare. 자원이 수요에 비해 부족한 상태

det.analysis:
❌ ① adequate (적절한, 충분한) — 충분하면 세 가지 모두 할 수 있어 but과 모순
✅ ② insufficient (불충분한) — 세 가지 모두 하고 싶지만 시간이 부족하다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ excessive (과도한) — 시간이 과도하면 선택할 필요가 없음
❌ ④ unlimited (무한한) — 무한한 시간이라면 모든 것을 할 수 있음
det.tip: insufficient = not enough. adequate(충분한)의 반의어

det.korean: 목적 A의 충족(만족)을 더 높이 평가했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① satisfaction (만족, 충족) — 목적 A의 충족을 B나 C보다 높이 평가했다는 원문 맥락에 정확히 부합 ←정답
❌ ② completion (완성) — 유사하나 원문은 satisfaction 사용. '완성'보다 '충족/만족'이 경제학적 맥락에 적합
❌ ③ achievement (성취) — 목적의 달성이 아닌 충족도를 비교하는 맥락
❌ ④ fulfillment (실현) — 유사하나 원문은 satisfaction. ends의 충족 순위를 매기는 맥락
det.tip: satisfaction of ends = 목적의 충족/만족. 경제학에서 효용의 개념과 연결

det.analysis:

❌ ② plentiful (풍부한) — scarce의 반의어
✅ ③ rare (드문, 부족한) — scarce의 동의어. 양이 적고 구하기 어려운 의미 ←정답
❌ ④ ample (충분한) — scarce의 반의어
det.tip: scarce = rare = insufficient. 모두 '부족한, 드문'의 의미

❌ ③ declines (감소하다) — 다른 의미. 줄어드는 것
❌ ④ settles (해결되다, 정착하다) — 발생이 아닌 해결의 의미

questions.passage:
(A) Action takes place by choosing which ends shall be satisfied by the employment of <u>means</u>.
(B) What she <u>means</u> is that we should focus more on quality than quantity.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 means가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 수단의 사용을 통해 행동한다. (B) 그녀가 의미하는 바는 품질에 집중해야 한다는 것이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 방법 — 수단: (A)가 수단인 것은 맞으나 방법과 수단을 구별해야 함. (B)는 동사 '의미하다'
❌ ② 의도 — 방법: 두 문맥 모두 해당하지 않음
❌ ③ 수단 — 수단: (B)는 동사로 쓰여 '의미하다'의 뜻
✅ ④ 수단 — 의미하다: (A) means = 수단(명사, 목적 달성을 위한 도구). (B) means = 의미하다(동사, what she means) ←정답
det.tip: means: 명사 '수단/방법' vs 동사 mean의 3인칭 단수 '의미하다'

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "not enough to meet a need or requirement; lacking in quantity or quality"

det.korean: 필요나 요구를 충족시키기에 부족한; 양이나 질이 모자라는.
det.analysis:
❌ ① adequate (적절한, 충분한) — 정의의 반대. 필요를 충족하는
✅ ② insufficient (불충분한) — 필요를 충족시키기에 부족하다는 정의에 정확히 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ excessive (과도한) — 부족이 아닌 과잉
❌ ④ abundant (풍부한) — 정의의 반대. 양이 많은
det.tip: insufficient = not sufficient = not enough. 수요에 비해 공급이 부족한 상태

questions.passage: When we must use a means so that some ends remain unsatisfied, the __________ (necessary) for a choice among ends arises.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: necessary → necessity (형용사 → 명사 변환). the + __________ + for 구조에서 관사 the 뒤에 명사가 필요. necessary(형용사: 필요한) → necessity(명사: 필요성). 'the necessity for ~' = '~의 필요성'.
det.tip: necessary(형용사) → necessity(명사). the 뒤에 명사가 오는 패턴

questions.passage: For example, Jones is engaged in watching a baseball game on television. He is __________ (face) with the choice of spending the next hour in: continuing to watch the baseball game, playing bridge, or going for a drive.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 그는 다음 한 시간을 어떻게 보낼지 선택에 직면한다.
det.analysis: face → faced (과거분사 변환). 'be faced with ~' = '~에 직면하다'라는 수동태 관용구. be동사(is) 뒤에 과거분사 faced가 와서 수동태를 구성. 'face(직면하다)' → 'be faced with(~에 직면하다)'.
det.tip: be faced with = ~에 직면하다. face의 수동태 관용 표현. confront와 유사

questions.passage: Action takes place by choosing which ends shall be satisfied by the employment of means. Time is scarce for man only because whichever ends he chooses to satisfy, there are others that must remain unsatisfied. When we must use a means so that some ends remain unsatisfied, the necessity for a choice among ends arises. For example, Jones is engaged in watching a baseball game on television. He is faced with the choice of spending the next hour in: continuing to watch the baseball game, playing bridge, or going for a drive. He would like to do all three of these things, but his means (time) is insufficient. __________, he must choose; one end can be satisfied, but the others must go unfulfilled. Suppose that he decides on course A. This is a clear indication that he has ranked the satisfaction of end A higher than the satisfaction of ends B or C.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① For example (예를 들어) — 이미 Jones 예시가 끝나고 결론으로 이어지는 부분
❌ ② In contrast (반면에) — 대조가 아닌 인과관계
✅ ③ As a result (결과적으로) — 시간이 불충분하므로 '결과적으로' 선택해야 한다는 인과 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ In addition (게다가) — 추가 정보가 아닌 원인→결과 관계
det.tip: As a result = Consequently = Therefore. 인과관계를 나타내는 연결사

questions.passage: Action takes place by choosing which ends shall be satisfied by the employment of means. Time is scarce for man only because whichever ends he chooses to satisfy, there are others that must remain unsatisfied. He would like to do all three of these things, but his means (time) is insufficient. As a result, he must choose; one end can be satisfied, but the others must go unfulfilled. Suppose that he decides on course A. This is a clear indication that he has ranked the satisfaction of end A higher than the satisfaction of ends B or C.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① engaged in (~에 몰두하여, ~에 참여하여) — Jones가 텔레비전으로 야구 경기를 시청하고 있다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② tired of (~에 지친) — 피로가 아닌 활동 중인 상태
❌ ③ worried about (~에 대해 걱정하는) — 걱정이 아닌 시청 활동
❌ ④ familiar with (~에 익숙한) — 익숙함이 아닌 현재 활동 상태
det.tip: be engaged in = be involved in = participate in. '~에 참여/몰두하다'의 의미
